thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: 1845008879 - High OOM rate observed in serving-pool-a (5min error spike) :warning:
Maria (oncall): seeing repeated OOM / CudaError: out of memory on a few pods in serving-pool-a. errors spike started ~10m ago.
Devon: getting node flaps too? I see kube events showing CrashLoopBackOff and then node kubelet reporting memory pressure.
Maria (oncall): yes, three nodes flipped within 8m. attaching quick log sample: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:03:12Z] runtime: allocation failed: out of memory
E CudaError: out of memory (allocation 2097152)
containerd: oom kill invoked for pid 4217
```
Sam: any recent deploys to serving runtime or model changes?
Maria (oncall): no deploys in the last hour per deploy-bot. no config changes.
Jia: this smells like KV cache growth / fragmentation. we've seen slow memory creep from paged-attention allocator before.
Devon: agree. paging metrics show a steady increase in kv_page_allocated over the last day for pool-a, but not pool-b.
Maria (oncall): what immediate mitigations can we run to stop node flaps and get customer errors down?
OpsLead: steps: 1) drain a node and restart the runtime pods with KV cache cleared 2) toggle runtime flag to disable paged attention for large-context requests 3) rollback to last stable kernel for allocator debug if needed.
Sam: can we evict KV cache in-flight? we have an admin endpoint "/admin/kv/evict" but it needs to be called per-pod.
Maria (oncall): doing a script to call evict and restart one pod at a time. will post commands.
Maria (oncall): run: 
```bash
for p in $(rictl pods -l pool=serving-pool-a -o name); do
  curl -s http://$p:8080/admin/kv/evict && kubectl delete pod $p || true
done
```
Jia: before restarting, enable allocator debug malloc map on a test pod to capture fragmentation map: 
```bash
rictl exec -it pod/serving-runtime-xxxx -- sh -c 'echo 1 > /proc/sys/debug/allocator_verbose'
```
Devon: I'm going to cordon the most noisy node and move its pods gradually. cordon node-17 now.
Devon: cordon done. moving pods.
Maria (oncall): evict script started, restarting pods one by one. initial three restarted, memory nominal on those. error rate dropped from 7% to 2% per routing metrics.
incident-bot: NOTE: 1845008897 - Service degradation alert acknowledged by Maria (oncall).
Sam: customer impact? traffic router shows a 10% request drop to fallback model for customers using long-context endpoints. error rate for embeddings unaffected.
Jia: collecting nvprof and nvidia-smi output from a pod that OOMed for RCA: 
```bash
rictl logs pod/serving-runtime-crash | tail -n 200
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.free --format=csv
```
Devon: checked node metrics: page cache is high and fragmentation counters increasing (kv_frag_count). looks like allocator failing to coalesce freed pages under high churn.
Maria (oncall): any quick runtime config we can flip to reduce page churn?
Jia: we have a runtime flag `--kv-page-threshold` and `--paged-attn-enable`. set kv threshold higher to force eviction earlier and disable paged-attn for large requests. I'll push flags via rollout for pool-a only.
Sam: pushing flag change now to pool-a as a canary: 
```bash
rictl rollout set-config pool=serving-pool-a --kv-page-threshold=0.6 --paged-attn-enable=false --reason="emergency - mitigate kv drift"
```
Sam: rollout started (canary=1/5).
Maria (oncall): monitoring. within 3 minutes, memory allocation rate reduced. error rate down to 1.1%. good.
Devon: but note: disabling paged-attn increases latency + tokens cost for some workloads. should communicate to SRE and support.
OpsLead: posted an incident channel note to #customer-impact with short blurb.
sre-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-03-15-58. assigned to Maria, Devon, Jia.
Maria (oncall): collecting heap snapshots and nvcrash dumps for the pods that were OOMed. saving to s3://ri-incidents/1845008888/artifacts.
Jia: also enabling longer-term tracing for allocator: set env ALLOC_TRACING=1 on a debug replica. will attach flamegraphs.
Devon: customer impact: three paid customers reported 5-10% failed requests during 10:02-10:12 window; we sent automatic fallback to smaller model for some routes.
Sam: patching a temporary routing rule to send critical customers to dedicated pool-b to avoid further impact.
Maria (oncall): routing patch applied for customers [acme, zephyr] to pool-b. verified traffic switched.
Devon: ok nodes stabilized after rolling restarts and flags. we should keep paged-attn disabled until we fix fragmentation root cause.
Jia: early RCA hypothesis: a combination of increased small-request churn + a regression in allocator's free-path that prevented coalescing with paged attention enabled, leading to kv fragment growth and eventual OOM under peak.
OpsLead: follow-ups (owners): 
- Jia: deeper allocator heap analysis + backtrace correlation (owner: Jia)
- Devon: add guardrails to autoscaler to avoid concentrated densification in single pool (owner: Devon)
- Sam: postmortem draft + customer comms (owner: Sam)
